rules: Traducir SOLO los valores de texto al español, con un tono formal, médico, riguroso y pedagógico.
NO traducir identificadores, claves de objetos, ids de modalidad, nombres de archivo ni tags de código.

items.mri.name: Magnetic resonance imaging
items.mri.how: A 3-tesla magnet lines up hydrogen nuclei in water and fat. Radio pulses tip them over and the scanner listens as they relax. The pulse timing (TR, TE, TI) decides which tissue ends up bright.
items.mri.subs.t1.name: T1-weighted
items.mri.subs.t1gd.name: T1 + gadolinium
items.mri.subs.t2.name: T2-weighted
items.mri.subs.flair.name: FLAIR
items.mri.subs.dwi.name: Diffusion (DWI)
items.mri.subs.swi.name: Susceptibility (SWI)
items.mri.subs.dti.name: Diffusion tensor (DTI)
items.mri.subs.mra.name: MR angiography
items.mri.subs.asl.name: Perfusion (ASL)
items.mri.subs.mrs.name: MR spectroscopy
items.ct.name: Computed tomography
items.ct.how: An X-ray tube spins around the head while a detector ring measures how much each path is attenuated. Every voxel becomes a Hounsfield unit: air −1000, water 0, bone around +1000. The window decides which part of that range spans black to white.
items.ct.subs.ctb.name: Brain window
items.ct.subs.ctbone.name: Bone window
items.ct.subs.cta.name: CT angiography
items.pet.name: Positron emission tomography
items.pet.how: A radiotracer emits positrons that annihilate into paired 511 keV photons flying in opposite directions. The detector ring records these coincidences and maps where the tracer collects.
items.pet.subs.fdg.name: FDG (glucose)
items.pet.subs.amy.name: Amyloid
items.spect.name: Single-photon emission CT
items.spect.how: Gamma cameras rotate around the head and record single photons from the tracer. Coarser than PET, but some tracers lock in a snapshot of blood flow at the moment of injection.
items.spect.subs.hmpao.name: Perfusion (HMPAO)
items.spect.subs.dat.name: DaTscan
items.fmri.name: Functional MRI
items.fmri.how: Fast echo-planar scans every 2 seconds track the BOLD signal. Active neurons draw in oxygenated blood, which raises the MR signal by 1–3% about 5 seconds later. Statistics turn that into a colour map over an anatomy scan.
items.fmri.subs.bold.name: BOLD activation
items.eeg.name: Electroencephalography
items.eeg.how: Scalp electrodes pick up microvolt potentials from millions of cortical pyramidal cells firing in sync. Superb timing (milliseconds) but blurred location, because the skull smears the field.
items.eeg.subs.eeg.name: Scalp EEG (10–20)
items.meg.name: Magnetoencephalography
items.meg.how: Superconducting sensors in a helmet measure femtotesla magnetic fields from the same currents EEG sees. The skull does not smear magnetic fields, so sources can be localised to a few millimetres.
items.meg.subs.meg.name: MEG field map
items.us.name: Ultrasound
items.us.how: A transducer sends 2–7 MHz sound pulses and times the echoes. Bone blocks sound, so the brain is imaged through windows: the open fontanelle in babies, or the thin temporal bone in adults for Doppler.
items.us.subs.cus.name: Cranial ultrasound
items.us.subs.tcd.name: Transcranial Doppler
items.dsa.name: Catheter angiography
items.dsa.how: A catheter is steered from the groin to a neck artery and contrast is injected while X-ray frames are taken several times a second. A pre-contrast mask is subtracted so only the vessels remain.
items.dsa.subs.dsa.name: Digital subtraction
